summary: Ctrl+Backspacing a word with non-BMP characters in an edit box deletes additional characters
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft 1.20.2.
2. From the main menu, open Multiplayer.
3. Select Add Server.
4. Paste `𐑐 𐑑𐑑 𐑒𐑒𐑒 𐑓𐑓𐑓𐑓 𐑔𐑔𐑔𐑔𐑔 𐑕𐑕𐑕𐑕𐑕𐑕 𐑖𐑖𐑖𐑖𐑖𐑖𐑖` into the Server Address box.
5. Move the cursor to the end of the pasted string.
6. Press Ctrl+Backspace repeatedly.
7. Observe that deleting a word also deletes the preceding word instead of deleting only one word at a time.
Observed Behavior:
### Actual behavior

When the string contains non-BMP characters such as the Shavian characters in the reproduction, **Ctrl+Backspace deletes more text than the immediately preceding word**. The first press removes the word at the cursor and also removes part or all of the preceding word. Repeated presses therefore skip over multiple words instead of deleting exactly one word per press.

This occurs because the word boundary is calculated as a UTF-16 code-unit index, while the deletion offset is applied as a code-point offset. Each non-BMP character occupies two UTF-16 code units but is traversed as one code point, causing the deletion range to extend too far toward the beginning of the text.
Expected Behavior: When Ctrl+Backspace is used in an edit box containing non-BMP characters, it should delete only the single preceding word, including its associated spaces, and place the cursor at the resulting word boundary. Repeated presses should remove one preceding word per press without deleting any additional preceding words or characters, preserving the remaining text exactly.
